title: Using EQ at work, at home, in your community and beyond

say: Using EQ at work, at home, in your community, and beyond.
This is the video for module four of Emotional Intelligence for Daily Life.
For example, Patience sells hair products on Instagram from Benin City. A customer's order of 3 bottles of hair oil arrives with one broken, and she sends a voice note calling Patience a scammer.
Patience feels insulted. She uses STOP and waits 10 minutes before replying.

panel.heading: LAST: Patience calms an angry customer
items: Apologise: I am sorry this happened
Thank: thank you for telling me quickly

say: Listen. I hear you. You paid for 3 bottles and one arrived broken. That is very disappointing.

say: Apologise. I am sorry this happened. She does not argue about the word scammer.

say: Solve. Please send a photo. I will send a replacement with my rider tomorrow at no cost, and pack in bubble wrap from now on.

say: Thank. Thank you for letting me know quickly.
The customer leaves a positive review and orders again the next month.

panel.rule: Calm the feeling first. Then solving the problem is easier.

say: Feedback like you are careless judges the person. Even well done is too vague to learn from.

panel.heading: The SBI model: situation, behaviour, impact
right: Behaviour: kept looking at the phone

say: SBI keeps it fair. Say the situation: at the shop on Tuesday afternoon. The behaviour: when the woman asked about prices, you kept looking at your phone. The impact: she left without buying. Then ask for their view.
When you receive criticism, breathe, listen to the end, and ask for an example.

panel.heading: The SBI model: situation, behaviour, impact
right: Behaviour: kept looking at the phone

say: Strong feelings push poor money decisions. Many scams are built to make you feel fear. Your account will be blocked.

cards.d: Pay now or lose the offer.

say: Or greed. Double your money in 7 days.

cards.d: Pay now or lose the offer.

say: Or urgency. Pay now or lose the offer.

A rush of emotion around money is your signal to slow down. Never share your BVN, card PIN or OTP, and check with your bank on its official number. For any big decision in the red zone, wait 24 hours.

cards.d: Pay now or lose the offer.

say: For example, Adaeze and her husband Tunde both work in Lagos. Tunde sends money to his younger brothers, and Adaeze feels the household is left short.
On a calm Saturday she starts gently. I feel anxious about our savings when large amounts go out without planning. Can we sit down with the numbers?

card.title: Adaeze and Tunde agree a money plan

say: Tunde explains his need. As the first son, supporting his brothers matters deeply to him. Adaeze shares hers: security for their own children. They write their combined income, about 650,000 naira.

card.title: Adaeze and Tunde agree a money plan

say: They put 50,000 naira into savings first, and agree a fixed 80,000 naira a month for family support.

card.title: Adaeze and Tunde agree a money plan

say: Any extra request above 20,000 naira, they discuss together first. The difference in values remains, but the monthly fight stops.

rows: Talk first if an extra is above

say: For example, Folake chairs a women's thrift cooperative in Ilorin. Two members quarrel in the WhatsApp group about missed contributions. Folake posts: let us not discuss this here. I will meet you both on Saturday.

panel.heading: Folake mediates a cooperative quarrel
items: Move it out of the group chat
Each tells her side; reflect feelings

say: At the meeting she sets rules. One person speaks at a time, no insults.

panel.heading: Folake mediates a cooperative quarrel
items: Move it out of the group chat

say: Each tells her side, and Folake reflects their feelings. Kafayat feels it is unfair. Mama Sade is embarrassed, because flooding closed her shop for a month.

panel.heading: Folake mediates a cooperative quarrel
items: Move it out of the group chat
Each tells her side; reflect feelings

say: Both want the cooperative to survive and stay trusted.

say: Mama Sade agrees to repay in four weekly instalments, recorded by the treasurer, and the group writes a clear rule for missed payments.

say: Emotional intelligence grows with practice and fades without it. Choose two skills: one about you, and one about others.
For example, Esther, a nurse in Jos, chose self-regulation and speaking up instead of going quiet.

panel.heading: Your 30-day plan
items: Week 4: review and ask for feedback

say: Her daily habit was 4 rounds of box breathing in the car after each shift, before entering the house.

panel.heading: Your 30-day plan
items: Week 4: review and ask for feedback

say: Each week built on the last. After 30 days her husband noticed she came home calmer, and she planned a second 30 days.

panel.heading: Your 30-day plan
items: Week 4: review and ask for feedback

say: To remember. Use LAST with customers and SBI for feedback. Slow down when money stirs strong feelings.

Communication tools are for relationships where both people are safe. Hitting, threats or controlling all the money are abuse. Reach out to trusted family, a faith leader, the police or an organisation that supports women.

panel.heading: Remember
items: SBI feedback, then ask for their view
Strong feelings about money: slow down
Abuse is a safety issue: seek help
Two skills, 30 days, small daily habits
